segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Tonight I'm going to talk to you about that remarkable continent Antarctica - remote, hostile and at present uninhabited on a permanent basis.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: For early explorers, it was the ultimate survival contest; for researchers like me, it remains a place of great intellectual challenge; while for the modern tourist, it's simply a wilderness of great beauty.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: First, some facts and figures.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Antarctica is a place of extremes - the highest, coldest and windiest continent and over fifty-eight times the size of the UK.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The ice-cap contains almost 70% of the world's fresh water and 90% of its ice, but with very low snowfall, most of the continent technically falls unbelievably into the category of 'desert'!

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Huge icebergs break off the continent each year, while in winter half the surrounding ocean freezes over, which means its size almost doubles.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Research and exploration has been going on in Antarctica for more than two hundred years, and has involved scientists from many different countries, who work together on research stations.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Here science and technical support have been integrated in a very cost-effective way - our Antarctic research programme has several summers-only stations and two all-year-round ones; I was based on one of the all-year-round ones.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The research stations are really self-contained communities of about twenty people.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There's living and working space, a kitchen with a huge food store, a small hospital and a well-equipped gym to ensure everyone keeps fit in their spare time.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The station generates its own electricity and communicates with the outside world using a satellite link.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Our station - Zero One - had some special features.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It wasn't built on land but on an ice-shelf, hundreds of metres thick.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Supplies were brought to us on large sledges from a ship fifteen kilometres away at the ice edge.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Living in the Antarctic hasn't always been so comfortable.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Snow build-ups caused enormous problems for four previous stations on the same site, which were buried and finally crushed by the weight.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Fortunately no-one was hurt, but these buildings became a huge challenge to architects who finally came up with a remarkable solution - the buildings are placed on platforms which can be raised above the changing snow level on legs which are extendable.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Food is one of the most important aspects of survival in a polar climate.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: People living there need to obtain a lot more energy from their food, both to keep warm and to undertake heavy physical work.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Maybe you know that an adult in the UK will probably need about I, 700 kilocalories a day on average; someone in Antarctica will need about 3.500 - just over double!

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This energy is provided by foods wpich are high in carbohydrate and fat.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Rations for fieldwork present an additional problem.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They need to provide maximum energy, but they must also be compact and light for easy transport.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Special boxes are prepared, each containing enough food for one person for twenty days.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You may be familiar with coffee processed by freeze-drying, which preserves the quality of the food product while making a large saving in weight- well, this type of presentation is ideal in our situation.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It wasn't available to earlier polar explorers, whose diet was commonly insufficient for their health.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I think that being at the cutting edge of science has a special appeal for everyone working in Antarctica, in whatever capacity.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: As a marine biologist, my own research was fascinating; but it's perhaps climate change research that is the most crucial field of study.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Within this general field, surveying changes in the volume and stability of the ice-cap is vital, since these may have profound effects on world sea levels and on ocean currents.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: A second important area is monitoring the size of the hole in the ozone layer above Antarctica, since this is an indicator of global ultra-violet radiation levels.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Thirdly, bubbles in the ice-sheet itself provide an index of pollution because frozen inside them are samples of previous atmospheres over the past 500,000 years, and these provide us with evidence for the effects of such human activities as agriculture and industry.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There are an increasing number of opportunities for young people to work for a period in Antarctica - not only as research assistants in projects like mine, but also in a wide range of junior administrative and technical positions including vacancies for map-makers.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I hope that the insights I've provided will encourage you to take up these opportunities in this fascinating continent.
